answer: Each identity locks 70 credits and files one ferrous lot and its pigment output. Conversion is fixed at 10 ferrous units to 1 pigment unit, so claimed pigment must equal input divided by 10. A jade auditor recomputes the public equation per identity and burns the bond on mismatch. Each lot hash counts once, so reuse leaves extra identities short. The kth fake pays 70 plus 15 fee plus 20 for a fresh lot; 1,000 fakes cost 105,000, with no bulk discount. A rented-lot ring fails because the reused hash counts once and the extra identities burn. Honest identities pay once and reclaim the bond.
